description: The Nature-Based Solutions Opportunity Scan is a World Bank screening method that uses Earth observation data to find where nature-based solutions could reduce disaster risk and build climate resilience, as the start of an investment plan. It covers a city or coastline per application in about six weeks, working through four steps: mapping the magnitude of hazards and resilience challenges, finding suitable areas for each solution type, estimating benefits, and choosing an investment mix by multicriteria or cost-benefit analysis. It was developed by the Global Program on Nature-Based Solutions for Climate Resilience of the Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery; the programme page shows an urban application in Dakar (pluvial flooding, heat and green space access, with bioretention areas, urban forests and green roofs) and a coastal application in Timor-Leste (coral reefs, mangroves and sandy beaches). The results are available as interactive maps on the page; the scan itself is a service designed for World Bank operations, requested through the programme's contact, and no licence is stated. Caveats: no software or data is released for independent use. It informs climate adaptation investment planning that blends green and grey infrastructure; a related record is the global dataset of nature-based solution opportunity areas for infrastructure.
